title: Transport Networks
summary: Types of transport and their advantages and disadvantages, transport networks and corridors in South Africa, and how transport affects development.

notes.text: **Transport** moves people and goods from one place to another. Good transport links help farms, mines and factories get raw materials and send products to markets, and let people reach jobs, schools and hospitals. A **transport network** is the system of routes (roads, railways, air and sea routes) and the places (nodes) they connect.

items: **National roads** (N1, N2, N3 and others) link the main cities. The **N3** between Durban and Johannesburg is one of the busiest freight routes in Africa.
**Railways** run by Transnet carry coal from Mpumalanga to **Richards Bay** and iron ore from Sishen to **Saldanha Bay**.
**Major ports**: Durban (the busiest container port in sub-Saharan Africa), Cape Town, Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha), Ngqura, East London, Richards Bay and Saldanha Bay.
**Airports**: O. R. Tambo International (Johannesburg), Cape Town International and King Shaka International (Durban).
The **Maputo Development Corridor** links Gauteng with the port of Maputo in Mozambique.

notes.text: A transport route (road, rail and often pipelines and power lines) along which economic development is encouraged, linking areas of production with ports and markets.

notes.title: Choosing a mode of transport
notes.problem: Which transport suits (a) millions of tonnes of coal going from Mpumalanga to Richards Bay and (b) fresh flowers going overseas?
steps: (a) Coal is heavy, bulky and not urgent, so rail is cheapest.
(b) Flowers are light, valuable and spoil quickly, so air is best despite the high cost.

notes.text: Places with good transport links attract industries and grow; isolated rural areas often remain poor because it is expensive to reach markets and services. Many South Africans depend on **minibus taxis**, which carry most commuters, followed by buses and trains.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: When choosing the best type of transport for a product, think about **weight/bulk**, **value**, **how quickly it spoils**, **distance** and **cost**.

notes.title: A new road to a village
notes.problem: A tarred road reaches a remote village. Give one benefit and one possible problem.
steps: Benefit: farmers can sell goods in town, and clinics and schools are easier to reach.
Problem: more traffic and accidents, and local shops may lose customers to the town.
notes.answer: Better access to markets and services, along with more traffic and competition.
